title: What is known about 1RB1LC_1LA1RF_0RD1RD_0RA0LE_1LA0LE_0RC---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LC_1LA1RF_0RD1RD_0RA0LE_1LA0LE_0RC---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Four shift rules of the crossings are proved in Lean for all sizes (lean/Rules.lean); the motion of the marks and the merges are only described from simulation.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 22,729 cells have been visited and 13,269 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.1). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.493).

claims.title: Crossings of the runs
claims.text: D crosses 010 words to the right and restores them to 110; E crosses 110 words to the left writing 010, and 011 words writing 001; C crosses 001 words to the right restoring 110.

claims.title: Marks move through the runs and merge
claims.text: At the moments the tape grows on the right it reads d^x 0 0 1 1 d^y M d^z ... (d = 110, M another mark). Between such moments the mark 0 0 1 1 moves right by a fixed number of words (8 per round around step 1.2·108, with z growing by 2), so x + y stays fixed within a phase; when y reaches 0 the marks merge and a new phase starts with x small. The sum x + y at the start of a phase went 25, 44, 64, 94, 147, 196, 204, 272, 325, 425, 459, 688, 785, 993, 1203, 1409, 1899, 2073, 2507 (step 1.5·108).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The halting transition is F1, and F is entered only from B reading a 1 (1RF), so a halt needs B> 1 1. A crossing never does that, so a halt could only come at a merge of two marks. The merges have not been worked out.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The tape is long runs of the word 110 with a few marks in between. The head shuttles between the marks and the right end, and each shuttle carries a mark a little further right. When a mark reaches the next one, the two merge and a new, longer phase starts. The crossings are proved in Lean; the merges are not worked out.

facts.text: Shift rules over runs of 3-cell words, proved for all lengths.
Length of the main run, in words, at the phase start at step 1.5·10<sup>8</sup>.
No halt in the C simulator.

sections.eyebrow: What the tape is made of
sections.heading: Runs of 110 and travelling marks
html:
Write d for the word 110. Each time the tape grows on the right it reads something like

d^607 0 0 1 1 d^1899 1^6 d^149 1 1 d^2 1 1 d 1^4 d^2 1 0 [A>]

(step 117,127,344): long runs of d, a mark 0 0 1 1, more marks, and the head at the right end. The head shuttles between the marks and the right end. On the way it re-encodes the runs it crosses, 110 into 010 or 011/001 and back, and these crossings are the four shift rules in lean/Rules.lean. In this example, after one round of about 2.2·105 steps the tape reads d^615 0 0 1 1 d^1891 1^6 d^151 ...: the mark has moved 8 words to the right and the run after 1^6 has gained 2.

sections.heading: Phases
html:
So within a phase x + y is fixed and the mark crosses the run at a steady rate, while the runs further right grow. When y reaches 0 the mark meets the next one, the marks merge, the runs are redistributed and a new phase starts with x small. The length x + y of the main run at the start of each phase went

25, 44, 64, 94, 147, 196, 204, 272, 325, 425, 459, 688, 785, 993, 1203, 1409, 1899, 2073, 2507 (step 1.5·108),

so the phases grow by irregular factors between about 1.04 and 1.8. The rate at which a mark moves (8 or 16 words per round in the phases looked at) and what a merge produces depend on the marks further right: a nested, Collatz-like counter.

sections.heading: Where a halt would have to come from
html: The only halting transition is F on a 1. F is entered only from B reading a 1, so a halt needs the head in state B on 1 1. The crossings never do that; a halt could only come at a merge. The next step is to list the marks, prove one round and each merge with symtm, and turn them into a map on the run lengths (see the README).

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.1). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.493).
After 109 steps the tape spans 22,729 cells (118 left of the start, 16,970 right), with a density of 1s of 0.584.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Long runs of the word d = 110 with a few marks between them (0 0 1 1, 1 0 1 1, 1^6, ...). The head shuttles between the marks and the right end, and each shuttle moves a mark a few words to the right; when a mark reaches the next one they merge and the runs are redistributed, a nested counter whose phases grow irregularly.
